stem:
A series of reactions for phosphorus and its compounds is shown.

$$\text{P} \xrightarrow[\text{reaction 1}]{\text{excess }\text{Cl}_2} \text{PCl}_5 \xrightarrow[\text{reaction 2}]{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 \xrightarrow[\text{reaction 3}]{\text{NH}_3} (\text{NH}_4^+)(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-)$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what you would observe in reaction 1.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the type of reaction that occurs in reaction 2.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ can be produced by direct reaction of phosphorus with nitric acid.

$$\text{P} + 5\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O} + 5\text{NO}_2 + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$

Use oxidation numbers to show that this reaction is a redox reaction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Reaction 3 is a neutralisation reaction in which $\text{NH}_3$ acts as a base.
parts.text: Explain how $\text{NH}_3$ acts as a base in reaction 3.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the three-dimensional shape of the ammonium ion, $\text{NH}_4^+$. Give the bond angle.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State the industrial importance of compounds such as $(\text{NH}_4^+)(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-)$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{PCl}_5$ can be used to convert alcohols to halogenoalkanes.
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ with $\text{PCl}_5$ to form $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the type of reaction in (i).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Halogenoalkanes can also be prepared by reacting alcohols with hydrogen halides, such as $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HI}$.

- $\text{HCl}$ is prepared using $\text{NaCl}$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
- $\text{HI}$ is prepared by reacting $\text{NaI}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$.

Suggest why $\text{HI}$ is not prepared by the reaction of $\text{NaI}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:
The rate of the hydrolysis reaction of halogenoalkanes with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ is dependent on the halogen that is bonded to carbon.

State and explain the order of reactivity when $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ reacts separately with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{I}$.
